channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-12
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 114 news received.

item.title: OpenAI lets businesses claim their ChatGPT profile
item.description: OpenAI is testing a Businesses feature that lets companies manage their profile in ChatGPT, update their information and track interactions. Business Hub also allows them to add product catalogs and view mentions, views and clicks.

item.title: Jensen Huang could be ousted from Nvidia
item.description: Nvidia’s board is reportedly preparing to remove Jensen Huang from his position following revelations about a new affair. His departure could seriously disrupt Nvidia, the AI market and Anthropic’s IPO plans.

item.title: Companies are banning artificial intelligence agents
item.description: Some companies are banning AI agents. The article lists the companies involved.

item.title: Panel publishes OpenAI’s Lean proof on Yang-Mills theory
item.description: David Gross’s panel published OpenAI’s Lean proof establishing the existence of pure Yang-Mills theory and said its checks support it. The question of whether a mass gap exists remains open.

item.title: Google, Anthropic and OpenAI add new tools to their AI products
item.description: Google, Anthropic and OpenAI have each added tools designed to move more tasks into their AI products, including Claude’s shared spreadsheets and ChatGPT’s professional agents.

item.title: Mathematicians seek to preserve their profession as AI advances
item.description: Artificial intelligence is now advancing into high-level mathematical research, forcing the community...

item.title: Claude takes on Microsoft Office with new professional tools
item.description: Anthropic is launching new Claude tools for office work, including Meetings, Whiteboards, Sheets and Data. Claude Meetings can join videoconferences and perform tasks such as creating a timeline or searching for figures.

item.title: OpenAI losses soar despite sharp revenue growth
item.description: OpenAI generated 10 billion dollars in revenue in the third quarter, but its operating loss reached 10.9 billion dollars. Revenue rose 50% from the previous quarter and tripled year over year.

item.title: SpaceX launches Starlink Mini 2 with removable battery and Wi-Fi 6
item.description: SpaceX has launched the Starlink Mini 2, featuring a removable battery and Wi-Fi 6.

item.title: TSMC invests up to one billion dollars in Anthropic and OpenAI
item.description: TSMC plans to acquire stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI worth up to one billion dollars.

item.title: Nvidia H200 AI chips reach blacklisted Chinese university
item.description: Nvidia H200 artificial intelligence chips have made their way to a Chinese university on a blacklist.

item.title: A Model Y owner looks back on another summer season
item.description: The title presents a review of another summer season with a Tesla Model Y.

item.title: Road noise and seals on the Tesla Model 3
item.description: The title presents a discussion about road noise and the seals on the Tesla Model 3.

item.title: ChatGPT Enterprise arrives on AWS Marketplace
item.description: OpenAI now offers ChatGPT Enterprise through AWS Marketplace, with purchasing, management and billing handled through existing AWS accounts. Customers can use their AWS commitments and access specialized offerings for healthcare and finance.

item.title: Anthropic and OpenAI seek greater control over software development
item.description: Anthropic and OpenAI are expanding their features to handle more of the end-to-end software development process. The shift aims to increase the profitability and commercial value of their models.

item.title: U.S. futures decline before the open
item.description: U.S. stock futures fell Thursday as turmoil at Nvidia worsened.

item.title: December 23 could be the ideal day to buy a home
item.description: The Christmas period can be especially favorable for homebuyers. One agent specifically recommends making an offer on December 23.

item.title: Wall Street fears the Fed may go too far against inflation
item.description: The high October CPI report prompted some Fed officials to adopt a tougher tone. One governor said he favored a 50-basis-point rate hike.

item.title: Investor bets on recycling data center materials
item.description: Tazia Smith, CEO of Closed Loop Capital Management, sees opportunities in companies that help data centers reuse raw materials from their supply chains.

item.title: Standard Bots aims to build America’s robotics giant
item.description: Standard Bots CEO Evan Beard wants to compete with Chinese robot manufacturers. He is counting in part on vibe coding and support from Washington.

item.title: Google lets employees test its Gemini Hydrogen model
item.description: Google is allowing employees to test Hydrogen, a new Gemini model described as faster and more cost-effective. One employee compares it with the company’s earlier Flash models.

item.title: Hacker houses are creating their own venture capital funds
item.description: Hacker houses want to invest in future unicorns before traditional venture capital funds do. Two former Mission Control roommates launched Mission Street Capital.

item.title: Deloitte cuts GLP-1 drug coverage for employees
item.description: Deloitte is reducing coverage for GLP-1 weight-loss drugs for its U.S. employees. The company is also increasing the cost of their health insurance.

item.title: Video game publishers benefit from the return of classic franchises
item.description: New Legend of Zelda and World of Warcraft games generated record results for Nintendo and Blizzard. Preorders for Grand Theft Auto 6 also exceeded expectations.

item.title: Rent exceeds 30% of income in 31 U.S. states
item.description: In Hawaii and New York, rent accounts for about half of income, compared with roughly 21% in North Dakota. Affordability pressures are spreading beyond traditionally expensive regions.

item.title: Miss Universe controversies ahead of TLC documentary
item.description: The article recaps the controversies surrounding Miss Universe ahead of the release of TLC’s new documentary series, Crown of Deceit.

item.title: Alex Karp says Palantir is a progressive company
item.description: Alex Karp describes himself as a lifelong Democrat and says Palantir’s products are “essentially progressive.”

item.title: Elon Musk’s exercise for identifying talent
item.description: The article presents the exercise Elon Musk uses to identify talent and explains how to apply it to demonstrate one’s impact at work.

item.title: The ten U.S. states that will build the most homes
item.description: The article presents the ten U.S. states expected to build the most homes in the coming years.

item.title: Tesla will extend Cybertruck production through the end of summer
item.description: Elon Musk said Tesla would extend Cybertruck production through the end of summer.

item.title: Amanda Seyfried does not regret her scene with Billy Evans
item.description: Amanda Seyfried said she has no regrets about her confrontation with Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’s partner, in a memorable scene.

item.title: Meghan Markle’s relationship with her father explored in detail
item.description: The article traces the relationship between Meghan Markle and her father, Thomas Markle.

item.title: United bars third-party AI agents from booking flights
item.description: United has restricted access to its app, website, agencies and comparison sites for unauthorized third-party AI agents. The airline cites exposed credentials, accidental purchases and booking errors, among other concerns.

item.title: DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2 to predict the effects of DNA mutations
item.description: AlphaGenome 2 predicts which cells are affected by a single-point DNA mutation, taking cell type or state into account. The model was trained on more than 100 million cell profiles from 68 tissues, but remains intended for research and is not validated for clinical or diagnostic use.

item.title: xAI abandons JAX for a C/C++ stack ahead of Grok 4.8’s deployment
item.description: Elon Musk says xAI has replaced JAX with an internally developed C and C++ stack. Grok 4.8 is undergoing reinforcement learning ahead of a phased rollout announced for this week.

item.title: IBM reaches new milestones toward its Starling quantum computer
item.description: IBM says it has reached major milestones toward Starling, its fault-tolerant quantum computer planned for 2029. The company notably connected two chips with a 1% error rate.

item.title: Meta dramatically speeds up the k-means clustering algorithm
item.description: Meta researchers updated k-means to achieve lower error in 1.4 to 2.6 passes instead of 25. They report 10- to 45-fold GPU speedups.

item.title: Microsoft announces Classroom, its autonomous education portal
item.description: Microsoft announced Classroom, an autonomous education hub bringing together assignments, grades and Copilot Teach. The service will arrive in 2027 at no additional cost for certain Microsoft 365 A2, A3, A5 and A7 customers.

item.title: Gemini Decisions API analyzes up to 1,000 questions about a file
item.description: Gemini Decisions API checks a photo, PDF or video against up to 1,000 questions in a single pass. For example, the service can evaluate 100 delivery photos against 16 criteria in 4.5 seconds.

item.title: AWS releases an open-source emulator written entirely by AI agents
item.description: AWS Emulator can run more than 200 AWS services on a laptop to test cloud code without an AWS account. The emulator was written entirely by AI agents and is open source.

item.title: ElevenLabs launches Scribe v3 with multilingual live transcription
item.description: Scribe v3 transcribes audio in 102 languages with 27% fewer word errors than version 2, according to ElevenLabs’ benchmark. Its Live version can now identify speakers in real time.

item.title: Grok Bot 1.0 adds shareable AI teammates to Slack and Teams
item.description: Grok Bot 1.0 offers shareable AI teammates in Slack, Microsoft Teams and meetings. They gradually learn how the team operates.

item.title: Tabletop turns group links and files into customized tools
item.description: Tabletop converts a group’s links, files and notes into customized tools, such as a seating plan or tournament bracket. The service is available through the Google Labs waitlist in the U.S. for people aged 18 and over.

item.title: Nod, n8n’s open-source personal agent, automates computer tasks
item.description: Nod is n8n’s personal agent, running on a Mac, Windows PC or server. It can follow up on unpaid invoices, cancel trials and prepare a briefing before a call; it is available as a free, open-source research preview.

item.title: Facade Code lets multiple coding agents collaborate in VS Code
item.description: Facade Code is a VS Code extension that runs Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents side by side in tabs. It also lets them communicate with one another and is released under the MIT license.

item.title: Switzerland must learn to worry despite its good health
item.description: Switzerland is doing well, but that may be precisely why it needs to learn to worry.

item.title: Trust and investment are essential to industrial survival
item.description: An industry does not disappear overnight: it first stops believing in itself and investing. By the time we realize it, it is often too late, in a world that is fragmenting.

item.description: Researchers at ETH Zurich have developed microrobots capable of improving the delivery of drugs to...

item.description: On December 8, 2026, from 1:30 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. at Station R in Renens, a meeting...

item.description: Researchers at ETH Zurich have developed a method for transforming waste plastic into...

item.title: Empa develops a new generation of antimalarial mosquito nets
item.description: Researchers at Empa have developed a new fiber for making impregnated mosquito nets...

item.title: Quantum vibrations pave the way for future molecular clocks
item.description: Researchers at the University of Basel have succeeded in observing and controlling quantum vibrations...

item.title: Basophils could slow down early lung metastases
item.description: Immune cells best known for their role in allergies could also contribute to...

item.title: A hot-spring amoeba pushes back the thermal limit of complex life
item.description: An amoeba discovered in a Californian hot spring has just broken a biological record...

item.title: Building your first AI automation
item.description: Chapter 28 explains how to choose a low-risk first automation, describe it with a trigger, an action and an outcome, then build and test an automatic morning briefing. Set aside 15 minutes and have the assistant connected to the previous chapter.

item.title: Five questions to identify tasks to automate
item.description: Chapter 29 proposes identifying repetitive tasks from a week of notes, then evaluating them with five questions, two of which can immediately eliminate a candidate. It also explains how to estimate the build cost and test the automation on a week that was already completed manually.

item.title: Apple to permanently shut down its support community
item.description: Apple will shut down its official Support Community forum, which will become entirely read-only before permanently closing on November 20. The company is inviting users to visit its official support website.

item.title: A Grok Build vulnerability exposes thousands of users’ secrets
item.description: Grok Build, SpaceXSI’s coding agent, exposed data belonging to thousands of users through shareable application links. The data included commercial projects, medical results and internal information.

item.title: Google Fi launches a “super network” that automatically chooses the carrier
item.description: Google Fi is launching a feature that lets phones automatically switch between two carriers to find the best signal. It is rolling out on Pixel 9 and later models with an eSIM, in more than 200 destinations.

item.title: Anthropic says AI is reducing Nvidia’s CUDA advantage
item.description: Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia’s advantage with CUDA and has reduced the switch from chips to AMD from several months to three days.

item.title: Regulator says evaluating academic work is nearly impossible with AI
item.description: A regulator says AI has made evaluating academic work “nearly impossible.”

item.title: Railway vulnerability leads to 740,000 dollars in AI-related charges
item.description: An intrusion targeting Railway resulted in 740,000 dollars in fraudulent charges for AI services.

item.title: Europe wants to ban deceptive interfaces and loot boxes for minors
item.description: Europe wants to ban “dark patterns” in apps, as well as loot boxes aimed at minors.

item.title: Kalshi warned of possible prosecution as authorities target prediction markets
item.description: Kalshi was reportedly warned of possible prosecution as federal authorities intensify their actions against prediction markets.

item.title: ByteDance reportedly preparing a Muse-inspired AI agent for the coming weeks
item.description: ByteDance is reportedly planning to launch an AI agent comparable to Muse in the coming weeks.

item.title: IBM ends visa and green card sponsorship for most consultants
item.description: IBM is ending visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting positions.

item.title: Microsoft discovers AI agents can be hacked by modifying their network
item.description: Microsoft discovered that AI agents could be compromised by modifying fewer than ten neurons.

item.title: Claris tests Harbor, a local AI app for Macs
item.description: Claris, an Apple subsidiary, is testing the Harbor app, designed to run AI locally on Macs.

item.title: AI agents discover an unmapped Maya site
item.description: AI agents have discovered a Maya site that was not shown on maps.

item.title: AMD launches EPYC Zen 6 processors for AI agent deployments
item.description: AMD has launched its EPYC Zen 6 chips, designed to enable denser deployments of AI agents.

item.title: The AI boom fills American RV parks
item.description: After the pandemic, the RV industry had weakened. The rise of data centers is reviving it by attracting workers to American RV parks.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 turns a prompt into a short film
item.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Fable 5.2, up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1 and available on paid Claude plans. Testers have used it to create videos and short animated films from a single prompt.

item.title: Instagram launches a free AI effects generator
item.description: Instagram’s Edits team has launched Effect Builder, a free web tool that turns a text description into an AI effect for Stories, without design or programming skills. The service is limited to the United States and people over 18.

item.title: Adobe and Disney partner to create custom AI models
item.description: Adobe and Disney have announced a multi-year partnership to create, through Firefly Foundry, generative models trained on Disney characters, environments, and visual styles. Walt Disney Imagineering is already using it for park design, including a model that transforms sketches into rendered 2D concepts.

item.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, a low-cost AI agent model
item.description: Meta has launched Muse Ember, its smallest model, which reportedly matches Claude Haiku 5.5 at about one-third of the per-task cost during agent steps run at scale.

item.title: Google unveils two new eighth-generation TPU chips
item.description: Google has introduced two new eighth-generation TPU chips, increasing pressure on Nvidia as competition for dedicated AI hardware intensifies.

item.title: Claude can audit your finances from CSV files
item.description: A creator demonstrates how to use Claude as a personal financial advisor by providing twelve months of bank transactions in CSV format. The process cleans the data, detects hidden subscriptions, and ranks expenses according to potential savings.

item.title: AARP publishes 12 tips for managing unwanted subscriptions
item.description: The guide covers monitoring price increases, setting calendar reminders, and what to do when a company refuses to cancel a subscription.

item.title: Apple explains how to cancel a subscription
item.description: The guide explains where to find each Apple charge so grouped line items can be linked to the relevant apps.

item.title: Google Play explains how to manage Android subscriptions
item.description: The help page explains how to cancel, pause, or change subscriptions billed through an Android phone.

item.title: The FTC directs users to ReportFraud to report recurring charges
item.description: The FTC’s ReportFraud website lets users report a charge that continues after a subscription has been canceled.

item.title: A free radio for listening to music in a Tesla
item.description: A Model Y owner recommends JSM Radio, which they use as their primary source of music in their car.

item.title: Can you accelerate while using autonomous driving?
item.description: A discussion considers whether it is possible to press the accelerator while Tesla’s autonomous driving is active.

item.title: Disable “Hey Grok” to avoid Grok surveillance
item.description: The discussion title recommends disabling the “Hey Grok” command to avoid being monitored by Grok.

item.title: A 12,318-mile cross-country trip in a Tesla
item.description: An owner recounts a 12,318-mile round trip across the country and the things that surprised them.

item.title: Discussion about energy consumption in Wh per mile
item.description: A discussion focuses on the energy consumption of Tesla vehicles, expressed in Wh per mile.

item.title: What is the best charging rate for a Tesla?
item.description: The title refers to a discussion about the best charging rate.

item.title: Should you leave the Tesla Wall Connector plugged in after 80%?
item.description: The discussion examines whether the Tesla Wall Connector should remain plugged in once the battery reaches 80%.

item.title: Scania goes from one person to 50 pilots through its customers
item.description: Scania’s Pilot Partner team launches a pilot only when a customer brings forward and funds a problem. This approach has helped deploy 400 electric buses in São Paulo and reshape the company’s strategy.

item.title: Supplier requests can reveal a deeper problem
item.description: An open innovation specialist was receiving mostly supplier requests from business units. During a discussion with five peers, she explored how to provide the requested supplier and then question the underlying need.

item.title: Six consumer-goods competitors share their pilots
item.description: AB InBev, Coca-Cola, Unilever, Danone, Colgate-Palmolive, and Mondelēz participate in the 100+ Accelerator. The program shares pilot results among its partners after one company defines the problem, funds the pilot, and evaluates its outcome.

item.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon available to the general public
item.description: After two weeks of limited availability to cybersecurity advocates, Gemini 4 Carbon is now accessible through Gemini, Search’s AI mode, Antigravity, or the API reserved for AI Ultra subscribers. Google says the model is particularly capable at complex, long-running tasks, precision knowledge, and data analysis.

item.title: How to choose the right AI model without exhausting your quota
item.description: Most labs offer three model tiers: a general-purpose model, a lighter version for simple tasks, and a more powerful version for ambitious projects. Anthropic’s guide recommends Opus 5.5 as a daily model, Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5 for simple tasks, and Fable 5.2 for complex projects.

item.title: An article examines why AI-generated texts are so frustrating
item.description: A new blog post examines in detail why readers dislike AI-generated texts and identifies three main flaws.

item.title: Anthropic shows a Fable-generated image that is hard to distinguish from a photograph
item.description: Anthropic asked its Fable model to create a painting presented as indistinguishable from a real photograph, then invited readers to determine whether the image was AI-generated.

item.title: Anthropic presents new experiments made with Fable
item.description: Anthropic published a new viral thread to showcase the capabilities of its latest Fable model.

item.title: A leadership lesson: helping your team overcome its fears
item.description: Bob Gilbreath recounts how an obstacle course organized with his team in 2015 strengthened the group’s confidence and led it to help a colleague overcome her fear. He encourages those who are hesitant to take the leap, also drawing on Joan Sotkin’s latest reflections on curiosity about oneself and change.

item.title: Microsoft opposes the U.S. ban on Chinese technology
item.description: Microsoft and industry groups oppose a proposed U.S. ban targeting Chinese optical transceivers used in data centers. They fear construction delays and unused AI chips due to a lack of sufficient alternative suppliers.

item.title: Panic over cloud capacity may be exaggerated
item.description: Claims that AWS and other cloud providers have sold all their AI capacity through 2027 overstate the shortages. Companies should distinguish between workload types, verify available capacity directly, and maintain flexible architectures.

item.title: IT leaders seek alternatives to SAP, VMware and Java
item.description: Rising license costs and support deadlines are prompting IT leaders to consider replacements for SAP, VMware and Oracle Java. However, integration, training and parallel-operation costs may exceed the license savings.

item.title: Cisco integrates Claude Mythos to test AI security
item.description: Cisco is integrating Anthropic’s Claude Mythos model into its AI Defense platform to improve adaptive security testing. The goal is to identify vulnerabilities and behavioral risks in AI agents within a controlled, authorized environment.

item.title: Google expands Gemini in Gmail to Workspace users
item.description: Google is extending email-thread summaries and the non-personalized “Help me write” feature to all Workspace users aged 18 and over. These features are enabled by default but can be disabled by users or administrators.

item.title: IBM expands Apptio tools to link AI spending with business value
item.description: IBM has expanded Apptio’s AI spending-tracking tools and Kubecost’s Kubernetes network cost reports. Features include AI usage connectors, financial planning, and greater visibility into certain AWS costs.

item.title: Docker Sandboxes isolate development environments
item.description: Docker Sandboxes provides isolated microVM-based development environments for building projects without cluttering the host system. Developers can create them with the sbx command, define network rules, and reproduce them using snapshots or declarative Dockerfiles.

item.title: Australian institution targets $2.1 million in savings with HPE
item.description: According to HPE, the Royal Australasian College of Surgeons cut its virtualization licensing bill by up to 70% and reduced its server fleet from eight to four. The organization expects total benefits of 2.1 million Australian dollars over five years.

item.title: CloudWatch Logs adds account-level retention policies
item.description: CloudWatch now supports retention policies that apply to an entire account or to log group prefixes.

item.title: Route 53 Profiles supports multiple profiles per VPC
item.description: Multiple Route 53 profiles can now be associated with the same VPC, allowing teams to manage separate DNS configurations with explicit priorities.

item.title: Purina turns smart feeder prototype into a connected product
item.description: Purina developed a cat feeder that identifies each animal and tracks its eating habits using vision, load sensors, and edge AI. With Edge Impulse, the team adapted its models to real-world household conditions.

item.title: Qualcomm launches RISC-V platform for connectivity and embedded AI
item.description: The Qualcomm QCC744-EVK platform, based on a RISC-V core, is now supported by Edge Impulse and Zephyr. It combines Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4, IEEE 802.15.4, local sensors, and machine learning for smart connected devices.

item.title: Industrial laundry automates defect sorting with edge AI
item.description: A laundry company deployed an Edge AI solution in three months using Edge Impulse’s FOMO vision algorithm to distinguish shadows from stains on fast-moving sorting lines. The system freed about a dozen employees for higher-value tasks.

item.title: Industrial prototype detects failures and coordinates repairs itself
item.description: A conveyor system combines anomaly detection, agentic AI, a unified namespace, and a VENTUNO Q board to detect abnormal vibrations locally, analyze the problem, initiate maintenance, and reschedule production. The prototype runs at the edge without relying on the cloud.

item.title: Magnetic sensor enables AI to recognize movements without a camera
item.description: A project uses a Hall-effect sensor, a Seeed Studio Wio Terminal, and a magnetic toy car to recognize fast, slow, or nonexistent movements without images. The model achieves 100% accuracy on the controlled test set and performs inference in under one millisecond on the terminal.

item.title: Robot plays rock-paper-scissors and taunts its opponent
item.description: A robot plays rock-paper-scissors by combining gesture detection, a language model, and speech synthesis, all running locally on a Qualcomm Dragonwing IQ9 EVK platform. A webcam and a robotic hand complete the interactive setup.

item.title: Arduino VENTUNO Q combines CPU, GPU, and NPU for edge AI
item.description: The Arduino VENTUNO Q board is designed for demanding applications such as advanced robotics and physical AI by combining CPU, GPU, and NPU capabilities. Its native support in Edge Impulse enables algorithms to be developed, optimized, and deployed directly on the board.
